from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(text_label, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(image_label, "B5")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = ["The forward process adds Gaussian noise.", "Pure static replaces the original image.", "The reverse process iteratively removes noise.", "Markov chains guide the image reconstruction.", "Finally, a clear image emerges."]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematics of Diffusion", lines)
        
        # Visual assets
        robot_img = Square(side_length=2, fill_opacity=1, color=BLUE).set_stroke(WHITE, width=2)
        noise_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=2, fill_opacity=0, color=GRAY)
        formula = MathTex(r"x_t = \sqrt{1-\beta}x_0 + \sqrt{\beta}\epsilon", font_size=32, color=GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(robot_img))
        self.place_at_grid(robot_img, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#808080"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(noise_rect))
        self.place_at_grid(noise_rect, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(noise_rect), FadeOut(robot_img))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Future Outlook", [
            "CLIP and Diffusion power modern AI.",
            "Latent models improve generation efficiency.",
            "This bridge transforms ideas into art."
        ])

        # Define assets
        clip = Text("CLIP", color=WHITE)
        diff = Text("Diffusion", color=WHITE)
        guid = Text("Guidance", color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(clip, 'B2', 0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(diff, 'B4', 0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(guid, 'B6', 0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(clip), FadeIn(diff), FadeIn(guid))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        line1 = Line(clip.get_right(), diff.get_left(), color=GREEN).set_opacity(0)
        line2 = Line(diff.get_right(), guid.get_left(), color=GREEN).set_opacity(0)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(line1), FadeIn(line2),
            line1.animate.set_opacity(1), line2.animate.set_opacity(1)
        )
        # Pulsing effect via updater
        line1.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.set_stroke(opacity=0.5 + 0.5 * np.sin(self.time * 5)))
        line2.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.set_stroke(opacity=0.5 + 0.5 * np.sin(self.time * 5)))
        self.wait(2)
        line1.remove_updater(line1.updaters[0])
        line2.remove_updater(line2.updaters[0])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        future_text = Text("Future: Unified Generative AI", color="#FFD700").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(future_text, 'E4', 1.0)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(
            FadeOut(clip), FadeOut(diff), FadeOut(guid),
            FadeOut(line1), FadeOut(line2),
            FadeIn(future_text)
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Text-to-Image AI: From Concepts to Pixels
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic background in linear algebra and probability

sections.title: Introduction: The Bridge between Language and Vision
sections.content: Explain the goal: How do we translate 'A fluffy cat wearing goggles' into a pixel array? Introduce the two core engines: CLIP (the translator) and Diffusion (the artist).
sections.example: Showing a text prompt on one side and a generated masterpiece on the other, connected by a symbolic 'AI Bridge'.

sections.title: CLIP: The Multimodal Semantic Compass
sections.content: Introduce Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP). Explain embedding space—mapping text and images into a shared high-dimensional vector space where related concepts sit closer together.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'semantic map' where the vector for 'dog' and a photo of a golden retriever converge at the same coordinate point.

sections.title: The Mathematics of Diffusion: Adding and Subtracting Noise
sections.content: Define the Forward Process (adding Gaussian noise until an image is pure static) and the Reverse Process (the learnable denoiser). Prerequisite: Mention that this uses Markov chains to gradually reverse entropy.
sections.example: A 3-step animation: A clear photo of a robot → Additive noise (dots) → Pure white static. Then, reversing the process to reconstruct the robot.

sections.title: The Denoising Engine: Integrating CLIP Guidance
sections.content: Explain how the model predicts the noise to subtract. The text-to-image integration occurs by using the CLIP vector to 'steer' the denoiser toward the regions of the image space that maximize the similarity between the generated content and the prompt.
sections.example: A 'steering wheel' icon overlaying the denoising process, shifting the image generation toward a 'cyberpunk city' style based on the CLIP embedding.

sections.title: Summary & Future Outlook
sections.content: Synthesize how these components function together. Conclude by mentioning the efficiency of modern diffusion models (like Latent Diffusion).
sections.example: A final visual flow chart: [User Text] → [CLIP Embedding] → [Diffusion Denoising] → [High-Res Image Output].
